title: Constant versus completed integral coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with ring of integers $\cO_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Work on the small pro-étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $R=(\cO_E)_X$ and $R_n=(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ for the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and put
$$B=\cO_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R_n$$
with its canonical map $c:R\to B$; the identification with the pulled-back integral coefficient sheaf is [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived extension of scalars [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $S=R$ or $B$, derived $\pi_E$-completeness means that the canonical map
$$M\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(M\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}R_n)$$
is an isomorphism; for $S=B$ this is [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. The canonical completion map and sequential derived limit use the functorial strict-tower model fixed in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]; its underlying homotopy limit is as in [def-weil-derived-limit].

1. $c$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and for every $n\geq1$ it induces an isomorphism
$$R_n=R/\pi_E^nR\xrightarrow{\sim}B/\pi_E^nB.$$
2. Restriction of scalars along $c$ is an equivalence from the derived $\pi_E$-complete objects of $D(B)$ onto the derived $\pi_E$-complete objects of $D(R)$, with inverse $L\mapsto$ derived completion of $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$.
3. For every $K\in D(B)$ and every $n\geq1$, the canonical finite-reduction comparison is an isomorphism
$$K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}R_n\cong (\operatorname{Res}_c K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R_n$$
in $D(R_n)$.

proof.text: Put $A=\cO_E$, $t=\pi_E$ and $I=(t)$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a principal ideal domain. Every ideal is therefore generated by one element, so $A$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use the small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ specified in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in the larger module universe; this is a small site for the general completion statements below. The identity $I^n=(t^n)$ identifies their finite constant sheaves with $R_n$. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], their completed ring sheaf $\widehat A$ is precisely $B$, including its finite projections and its map from $R$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $X$, and no invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$, has been introduced.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] to $T=X$, $A$ and $I$: $B$ is flat over $R$, and the projection induces $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R_n\simeq R_n$ for every $n\geq1$. Its degree-zero map identifies $B\otimes_R R_n=B/t^nB$ with $R_n$; flatness means there is no higher Tor here. For the source quotient, apply exactness of constant module sheaves in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties] to $0\to A\xrightarrow{t^n}A\to A/(t^n)\to0$: it gives $R/t^nR=R_n$. Both identifications use the quotient maps from $A$, so the induced map $R/t^nR\to B/t^nB$ is the inverse of the displayed projection isomorphism. This proves clause (1), with its specified canonical map.

proof.text:
With $A$, $I$, $R$, $\widehat A=B$ as in step 1, apply the finite-reduction clause of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] to an arbitrary $K\in D(B)$. It gives
$$\operatorname{Res}_c(K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R_n\simeq K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}R_n$$
in $D(R_n)$, not merely after forgetting the $R_n$-action. Taking its inverse proves clause (3). The cited statement also says that these comparisons are natural and commute with the maps $R_{n+1}\to R_n$, so the same identifications hold for the entire reduction tower.

proof.text: The equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], with the same $A$ and principal ideal $I$, is induced by $\operatorname{Res}_c$. Its last paragraph identifies local/Koszul-derived completeness with the condition that the canonical finite-reduction tower unit is an isomorphism, for both $R$ and $B$. This is precisely the completeness condition in the statement and, on $B$, [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. Moreover, restriction identifies those tower units and their derived limits. Therefore its equivalence is exactly between the two full subcategories in clause (2); this does not replace quotient-tower completeness by a different notion.

proof.text:
Write $r=\operatorname{Res}_c$ and $F=B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(-)$. On module sheaves the identity morphism of the underlying topos with ring map $c:R\to B$ gives $B\otimes_R(-)\dashv r$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Restriction is exact: the underlying abelian sheaf and its kernel and cokernel do not change when its scalars are restricted [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identify its everywhere-defined right derived functor with termwise restriction. The everywhere-defined left derived scalar extension is $F$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The derived adjunction theorem [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] consequently gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(F L,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(L,rM)$$
for arbitrary unbounded $L$ and $M$.

proof.text:
Let $C_B$ be derived completion on $D(B)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] with the single global section $t$ of $B$. It supplies a complete object $C_BN$ and natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(C_BN,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,M)$ for every complete $M$. By the Koszul/finite-quotient and unit comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], this reflector is the derived completion for the finite-reduction tower used here. For complete $L\in D(R)$ and complete $M\in D(B)$, its universal property and step 5 give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(C_B F L,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(F L,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(L,rM).$$
Thus $C_BF$ is left adjoint to the equivalence $r$ of step 4 on the complete subcategories. If $G$ is any quasi-inverse to that equivalence, full faithfulness gives $\operatorname{Hom}(GL,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L,rM)$, naturally in $L,M$. The two representing objects $GL$ and $C_BFL$ are therefore canonically isomorphic, naturally in $L$ (the isomorphism is obtained by evaluating the two Hom bijections on the respective identity maps). Consequently $C_BF$ is the inverse claimed in clause (2), with both compositions naturally isomorphic to the identity.
